👋 Thanks for opening this issue! I found a similar issue in our tracker that might address your problem: _[Issue weaviate/weaviate#4499: Dimensional consistency on batch is not being checked (Closed)](https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/issues/4499)_ _This closed issue is the closest match because it reports batch ingestion skipping vector validation and allowing invalid vectors through while single-object insertion correctly rejects them. It describes the same kind of batch-vs-singular validation inconsistency, though for vector dimensions rather than empty vectors._ Please check if this is the same issue. If so, consider adding your input there or closing this one. Thanks for helping us keep the issue tracker organized! 🚀 ---

body:
Thanks for the detailed report! After investigating, this is working as intended, and the "expected behavior" in the issue rests on a claim about the OpenAPI spec that doesn't hold. Details below.

1. The OpenAPI spec does not require a non-empty vector

The issue states the vector field is "documented as a non-empty float array (min_length=1)". That constraint does not exist. The object's vector field references C11yVector, which is a plain array of floats with no minItems/minLength:

- Spec definition: openapi-specs/schema.json → C11yVector (https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/blob/3bb5576a5f441f385cce3b7f158f0c9b0d54f1cc/openapi-specs/schema.json#L515-L521)
- A repo-wide grep for minItems/minLength in openapi-specs/ returns nothing.
- The generated validator C11yVector.Validate() (https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/blob/3bb5576a5f441f385cce3b7f158f0c9b0d54f1cc/entities/models/c11y_vector.go#L31-L33) is return nil — an empty vector is a valid value per the API contract.

2. An empty vector is intentionally treated as "no vector"

Vectors have been optional since #1800 (implemented in #1807). Throughout the codebase, an empty/nil vector means "this object has no vector":

- The object is stored, but is never inserted into the HNSW index — shard_write_put.go#L112-L116 (https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/blob/3bb5576a5f441f385cce3b7f158f0c9b0d54f1cc/adapters/repos/db/shard_write_put.go#L112-L116):
- Because it's not indexed, such an object will not match a nearVector query — so the "corrupts vector-search results" concern does not occur.
- Both the singular and batch paths call the same validator, vector_validation.go https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/blob/3bb5576a5f441f385cce3b7f158f0c9b0d54f1cc/usecases/objects/validation/vector_validation.go#L22-L71, which gates every error branch on len(vector) > 0 — an empty vector passes through by design.

3. Existing test confirms this is intended

TestUpsertToolInvalidVectorValues https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/blob/3bb5576a5f441f385cce3b7f158f0c9b0d54f1cc/test/acceptance/mcp/objects_upsert_test.go#L848-L878 feeds an explicit empty vector and deliberately accepts either success or failure — it does not require an empty vector to be rejected:


On the singular POST /v1/objects → 422 observation

On current main I could not find any path (swagger schema, usecase validator, or DB) that rejects a singular insert with vector: [] as 422 — the singular and batch paths share the same validation and both treat empty as "no vector". The 422 seen on v1.38.2 appears specific to that build/config rather than an intended contract.

Conclusion

POST /v1/batch/objects reporting SUCCESS for an item with vector: [] is intended behavior, consistent with the documented API (no non-empty constraint) and the optional-vector design (#1800). Closing as not a bug — happy to reopen if you can show the empty-vector object being returned by a nearVector search.

Related: #1800, #1807.
